---
title: Course guide
---

## Format

Each class combines approximately **50 minutes of theory** and **50 minutes of programming practice**. The emphasis is on intuition, economic applications, and tools useful for independent research. Python is the main language.

## Learning outcomes

By the end of the course, students should be able to implement numerical methods for dynamic economic models, use approximation and machine-learning tools, and document reproducible computational research.

## Assessment

The **replication project accounts for 100%** of the grade. Students may work in teams of 2–3; teams replicate as many papers as there are members. Evaluation emphasizes understanding, implementation, and reproducibility; exact reproduction of published results is not required.

See the [final project guide](project.qmd) for requirements and submission details.
